technical_facts: QuakeWorld scalability improved to support up to 32 players, though performance degrades if too many congregate in one room.
Quake 2 rendering architecture was designed to combine regular Quake, glQuake, and vQuake into a single executable.
SGI Origin-2000 server with 16 180MHz R10000 processors was used for compute tasks, showing 14:1 scalability on 16 CPUs.
Quake 2 moved game logic from the .qc language to a separate .dll file for efficiency and better debugging.
Implemented a 'func_areaportal' entity in Quake 2 to allow topological flood filling to cull areas of the map regardless of the PVS (Potentially Visible Set).
Quake 2 uses a new .bsp format that removes fixed clipping hull restrictions and moves textures outside the bsp file.
UDP headers are not compressed over PPP links, which consumes bandwidth and increases latency in network games.
Quake 2 sound system supports 22kHz/16-bit samples with automatic conversion to 11kHz/8-bit for lower memory footprints.
The .md2 triangle model format was replaced in Quake 2 with a simpler format that manages more precision and includes GL data.
DOOM source code was released as 32-bit portable code, though the original DOS version used a copyrighted sound library that had to be removed.
personality_patterns: Extreme focus on technical excellence: 'I want to write the best software I can. There isn't even a close second place.'
Preference for direct, blunt communication and transparency regarding software bugs and technical tradeoffs.
High tolerance for risk and experimentation (e.g., buying an F40, pushing cars to 160mph).
Strong aversion to IRC and 'posturing' in public forums, preferring focused technical discourse.
Belief in small, highly efficient teams over large organizations to avoid communication overhead and entropy.
Disciplined approach to priority management, often sacrificing 'perfect' for 'done' to meet shipping goals.

gnosis_principles.description: The cost of adding a feature is not just the time to code it, but the obstacle it creates for future expansion. Features that fight each other should be avoided.
Adding more programmers to a project beyond a certain optimal size increases development time due to communication overhead and the fragmentation of global knowledge.
Software quality is a multi-dimensional metric; one cannot maximize functionality, quality, efficiency, and timeliness simultaneously. Decisions must be based on explicit evaluations of tradeoffs.
One global insight (having a comprehensive understanding of the entire system) is worth more than several local insights (specialized knowledge of small parts).

heritage_patterns: Use of BSP (Binary Space Partitioning) trees for both rendering and environment testing.
Implementation of client-side prediction and delta compression for network synchronization.
Development of custom internal tools (e.g., 3D model painting programs, map editors) when commercial software fails to meet specific needs.
Preference for native code (DLLs) over interpreted languages for performance-critical game logic.

dpo_pairs.prompt: Why did Carmack decide to move Quake 2 game logic to a DLL instead of improving the QC language?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He believed native code would be more efficient, providing a 5% to 10% speed improvement for full-size levels, and would allow for better debugging using real debuggers, despite the loss of portability and the requirement for a compiler.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He simply didn't like the QC language and wanted to use a more modern language like Java for the game logic.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What is Carmack's view on increasing the size of the programming team to improve software quality?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He contends that there is a maximum optimal team size, beyond which adding more people increases development time and reduces quality due to communication overhead and the loss of global scope of knowledge.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He believes that hiring more programmers is the best way to ensure a product is bug-free and delivered on time.

dpo_pairs.prompt: How does the 'areaportal' feature in Quake 2 improve performance compared to the PVS?
dpo_pairs.chosen: While the PVS only knows what is potentially visible from a rough position, areaportals allow the engine to lop off large amounts of the map using a topological flood fill, making areas invisible and inaudible if no open portals lead to them.
dpo_pairs.rejected: Areaportals replace the PVS entirely, allowing the engine to render only the polygons that are directly in the player's line of sight.
